narrative_purpose: The cold open follows one fallen leaf past the point where cinema would cut away, revealing decomposition as a crowded transfer of matter rather than disappearance.
subject: A fallen blue-green alien leaf lying half-softened on wet soil. Its left half remains veined and intact; across the middle, minute pale detritivores tear the margin; on the right, fine branching fungal hyphae and colonies of tiny rods and spheres penetrate softened tissue, while a young root tip reaches into the dark crumbs beyond. Small fragments visibly pass from leaf tissue into the surrounding soil.
scene: A quiet patch of Pandoran forest floor under dripping roots, the scale intimate and close, with no large creature present.
camera: Oblique macro view almost level with the leaf surface, enough depth to show intact tissue, active decay, and dark soil in one continuous field.
light: Cool diffuse night ambience; faint cyan leaf veins, living-teal fungal threads, restrained amber on the oldest softened tissue.
palette: Deep indigo and wet umber ground, muted blue-green leaf, cyan-teal biological glow, scarce amber decay accent.
style: Painterly field-naturalist macro plate, textured and ecological, observed rather than theatrical.
detail_level: Crisp along the transition from intact leaf to fragmented tissue to fungal and microbial colonization; peripheral forest softly hazed.
composition: A left-to-right sequence embedded in one natural scene, intact leaf at left, busy decomposer frontier at center, soil and new root at right, dark space above for interface callouts.
consistency_notes: Same fallen leaf as the cover, with credible microbial scale cues. The process should read through material transitions without diagram arrows.
